title: Birth in 1902, non-musical family and hearing clarinet at picnics
summary: His parents and relatives did not play; he heard bands at picnics and wanted only to hear the clarinet.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Okay, that's where we're going. Let me start out with your name.
Now, just where were you born?
Oh, right here in New Orleans.
I was born in Priya and Allen. What was the date? March the 25th, 1902.
Were your parents musical? Did they play any instrument?
No. No, not that I know of. My father had a recording, but I don't think he ever played anything on it.
Any other relatives, uncles, or anybody else that ran city that played any instrument?
How did you get interested in music when you were a boy? What's your very first memory of remembering hearing music, bands, or singing, or what it was?

Well, I had a brother who used to get a lot of picnics out of Millen Boyd. And Mount Perez. You know when Nelson used to play for him. Quite natural when they'd have things like that, they had to carry the children along. So, I'd be out there and listening at the music.
And, uh, well the only thing my mind was on is the clarinet. That's all I wanted to hear. Mm-hmm. And, uh, well at them time, most of the time, it would be Lovin Nelson that was playing.
